# Testament of Asher — 10
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1:1** The copy of the testament of Asher, what he spoke to his sons in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life.
**1:2** For while he was still in good health he said to them: Hearken, ye children of Asher, to your father, and I will declare to you all that is upright in the sight of the Lord.
**1:3** God has granted two ways to the sons of men, and two inclinations, and two kinds of action, and two modes, and two issues.
**1:4** Therefore all things are by twos, one over against the other.
**1:5** For there are two ways of good and evil, and with these are the two inclinations in our breasts discriminating them.
**1:6** Therefore if the soul take pleasure in the good inclination, all its actions are in righteousness; and though it sin, it straightway repenteth.
**1:7** For having its thoughts set on righteousness, and casting away wickedness, it straightway overthroweth the evil, and uprooteth the sin.
**1:8** But if it incline to the evil inclination, all its actions are in wickedness, and it driveth away the good, and cleaveth to Beliar, and though it work what is good, it perverteth it to evil.
**1:9** For whensoever it beginneth to do good, he forceth the issue of the action into evil for him, seeing that the treasure of the inclination is filled with an evil spirit.

**2:1** A person then may with words help the good for the sake of the evil, and yet the issue of the action leadeth to mischief.
**2:2** There is a man who showeth no compassion upon him who serveth his lust in sin, and this involveth a twofold evil.
**2:3** And there is a man who loveth him that worketh evil; and this likewise is twofold in evil, since he followeth evil for the sake of his love, and yet suffereth him to go on in his evil.
**2:4** And there is a man who robbeth his soul from the necessaries of life, so that he may accomplish a good object; and in respect of this the apparent good is evil.

**3:1** Some call these things good who are really evil, and they perish in their sin; but others call them evil who are really good, while the end of the matter bringeth blessing to them.
**3:2** There are two sorts of men of two faces, but there is no truth in them.
**3:3** For the wicked are men of two faces: they do not serve God but their own lusts, so that they may please Beliar and men like unto themselves.

**4:1** For good men, even those who are of single face, though they be thought by those of double face to sin, are just before God.
**4:2** For many in killing the wicked do two works, of evil and good; but the whole is good, because he hath uprooted and destroyed that which is evil.
**4:3** One man hateth the merciful and unjust man, and the man who committeth adultery and fasteth: this also hath two faces, but the whole work is good, because he followeth the Lord's example, in that he accepteth not the seeming good as the truly good.
**4:4** Another desireth not to see a good day with those who revel, lest he defile his body and pollute his soul: this also is double-faced, but the whole is good.

**5:1** For such men are like stags and hinds, because in the manner of wild animals they seem to be unclean, but they are altogether clean; because they walk in zeal for the Lord and abstain from what God also hateth and forbiddeth by his commandments, warding off the evil from the good.
**5:2** But if the inclination of the soul be to evil, the whole of its action is evil; and though it do good it is in evil purpose; for the good and evil spirit are both met in it, and where the evil spirit prevaileth there also the good is perverted to evil.

**6:1** My children, therefore, observe all things in good order, for there is here a type set before you for repentance.
**6:2** Do righteousness upon the earth, that ye may have treasure laid up above; and sow good things in your souls, that ye may find them in your life.
**6:3** But if ye sow evil things, ye shall reap every trouble and affliction.
**6:4** Get wisdom in the fear of God with diligence; for if there be a captivity, and cities and lands be laid waste, and gold and silver and every possession perish, nothing can take away the wisdom of the wise, save the blindness of ungodliness and the dulness that cometh of sin.
**6:5** For if one keep himself from these evil things, then even among his enemies shall wisdom be a glory to him, and in a strange country a fatherland, and in the midst of foes shall prove a friend.

**7:1** And when he had said these things to them, he commanded them, saying: Bury me in Hebron.
**7:2** And he fell into a deep sleep and died.
**7:3** And afterwards his sons did as he had commanded them, and they carried him up to Hebron and buried him with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Asher*
